clue.text: Situation about which there's rejoicing when time isn't used for protest 23

indicators.note: the reduced word for rejoicing goes round the situation, which sits inside it
isn't used says the time letter is dropped from the word for rejoicing

parts.note: exultation is great rejoicing
a post is a situation or job

explanation.surface: A protest is staged at some happy occasion where the clock has been ignored.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop one T from EXULTATION to leave EXULATION, then 'about' wraps it round POST. The '23' in the held text is a stray from the print and plays no part.
explanation.definitionFit: An expostulation is a remonstrance, an earnest spoken objection, which is a protest.

clue.text: Body of text taken up with eccentric theory about power plant needing little water

indicators.note: in a down clue, taken up means the letters are read upwards, so backwards
the body of a word is its middle, without its first and last letters
the rearranged theory goes round the power letter
eccentric signals the letters of theory are put in an odd order

parts.note: P is the physics abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: A text is weighed down by a crank's theory about power.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle of 'text' is EX, turned upwards to XE. The letters of THEORY are rearranged round P to give ROPHYTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A xerophyte is a desert or dry-land species adapted to survive drought, such as a cactus.

clue.text: Acceptable to enter when? At the right moment

parts.note: on, as in 'that's not on', means acceptable
an actor's cue tells them when to come on stage

explanation.surface: Someone asks if it is all right to go in, and when.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To enter when?' is the question an actor's cue answers: the cue is the signal to come on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something on cue means doing it exactly when expected, at the proper time.

clue.text: Grass endlessly rising? Cutting it, I walk wearily

indicators.note: the I cuts into the reversed grass, so it sits inside it
in a down clue, rising means the letters are read from bottom to top
endlessly says the last letter of the grass is removed

parts.note: esparto is a tough grass used for making paper and rope

explanation.surface: Someone trudges wearily across a grass field that slopes upwards.
explanation.walkthrough: ESPARTO without its end is ESPART; 'rising' turns it to TRAPSE, and the I cuts into it.
explanation.definitionFit: To traipse is to trudge or tramp along tiredly.

clue.text: Graceful sequence from musical is so memorable

indicators.note: sequence from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A graceful scene from a musical that is memorable.
explanation.definitionFit: Lissome describes someone supple and lithe, moving with elegance.

clue.text: Not impossible to find fly in food

indicators.note: in says the word for fly is placed inside the word for food

parts.note: table can mean the food served, as in 'she keeps a good table'
to fly is to race or rush

explanation.surface: Someone spots a fly in their dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fly' looks like the insect but is the verb meaning to rush, RACE, put inside TABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something traceable can be tracked down or located.

clue.text: Elliptical lingo ultimately useless

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word lingo

parts.note: void means having no force, useless

explanation.surface: A complaint that roundabout jargon is pointless in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elliptical' suggests vague speech, which fits 'lingo', but here it means egg-shaped.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovoid means egg-shaped, an oval or elliptical form.

clue.text: Skill in most of language

annotationWithheld.why: Held as 'Skill in most of language (13)': HE(ART)BRE gives only HEARTBRE; the clue is cut short, missing the piece for AKING and the definition, and no reprint was found.

clue.text: Terms in which those are addressed

definitions.text: Terms in which those are addressed

parts.words: Terms in which those are addressed
parts.note: the words of greeting a minister uses to address the couple and congregation at the start of a church wedding

explanation.surface: A question of the correct way to address people.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is the opening of the Anglican marriage service: '... we are gathered here together'.
explanation.definitionFit: The words open the wedding service as the vicar's form of address to the assembled people.

clue.text: Top company with regret rejected Union officials

indicators.note: rejected says the whole string of pieces is turned back to front

parts.note: a star is a top performer
to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: A leading firm, sorry for itself, has been turned down by union officials.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union' looks like a trade union, but it is the European Union; 'rejected' turns STAR + CO + RUE back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: Eurocrats are the bureaucrats who staff European Union institutions.

clue.text: Trouble to occur with 25 building material

parts.note: ado means fuss or trouble
to be is to exist or occur

explanation.surface: Problems arise with some building material.
explanation.walkthrough: The '25' in the held text is a stray from the print and plays no part.
explanation.definitionFit: Adobe is sun-dried clay brick used for houses in dry regions.

clue.text: Amount of money you can make with right rug, wanting to

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the letters of to are removed

parts.note: rug is slang for a wig or hairpiece

explanation.surface: Someone proposes making money from the right sort of rug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rug' is slang for a hairpiece, TOUPEE; without TO it is UPEE, after R.
explanation.definitionFit: The rupee is the currency unit of India and Pakistan, a sum of cash.

clue.text: Fare paid without assistance by traveller, securing objective

indicators.note: without says the letters for assistance are taken from the word paid

parts.note: aid means assistance

indicators.note: securing means holding, so the traveller surrounds the objective

parts.note: a rover is a wanderer or traveller
an end is an aim or objective

explanation.surface: A fare paid by a lone traveller who keeps a goal in view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paid without assistance' looks like one idea but is PAID with AID removed, leaving P.
explanation.definitionFit: Provender is food or provisions, so it is fare in the sense of things to eat.

clue.text: Objection one made, losing 2 heart, about railway's latest delay

indicators.note: the string of pieces goes round the final letter of railway

parts.note: a but is an objection, as in 'no ifs or buts'

indicators.note: latest points to the last letter of the word railway

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: losing its heart says the middle letters of made go
losing its heart says the middle letters of made go

explanation.surface: A complaint about a railway's most recent delay.
explanation.walkthrough: MADE losing its middle is ME; BUT + I + ME goes round Y, the last letter of 'railway's'.
explanation.definitionFit: To buy time is to stall or put something off, gaining extra time.

clue.text: People entertained by prankster allowed to perform

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child or prankster

indicators.note: entertained means taken in as a guest, so the people go inside

parts.note: let means allowed
men can mean people in general

explanation.surface: People are amused by a joker who is permitted to put on a show.
explanation.definitionFit: To implement a plan is to carry it out or execute it.

clue.text: Mission that's mad may be stopped by saints

indicators.note: stopped by means plugged, so the saints are put into the rearranged letters
mad signals that the letters of may be are scrambled

explanation.surface: A crazy mission that saints might prevent.
explanation.walkthrough: MAY BE is rearranged to EMBAY, and SS plugs the gap.
explanation.definitionFit: An embassy is a diplomatic mission abroad.

clue.text: Upright icon hasn't changed

indicators.note: changed tells you to rearrange the letters of the two words

explanation.surface: An icon has stayed the same.
explanation.walkthrough: The ironic 'changed' is the anagram signal for ICON HASNT.
explanation.definitionFit: A stanchion is a vertical post or support.

clue.text: Disease of cereals certainly appearing in 4 record books

indicators.note: appearing in puts the word for certainly inside the record

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
yes is an affirmation meaning certainly
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: A crop disease is definitely in the record books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Books' is the Old Testament, OT.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyespot is a fungal infection of wheat and barley.

clue.text: Warship with value carrying king to the north and east

indicators.note: in a down clue, to the north means read upwards, so backwards
carrying means the value word holds the king letter

parts.note: merit means worth or value
R is short for rex, Latin for king
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A valuable warship carries a king north and east.
explanation.walkthrough: MERIT holding R is MERIRT; read upwards it becomes TRIREM, then E.
explanation.definitionFit: A trireme was an ancient galley with three banks of oars.

clue.text: Declare a goddess to be fair

parts.note: to aver is to declare
Ge, or Gaia, is the Greek earth goddess

explanation.surface: A goddess is declared beautiful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fair' looks like beauty but means middling.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair as in 'fair to middling' means ordinary or moderate.

clue.text: Note found beneath articles including large jumper?

indicators.note: found beneath in a down clue means the note comes after

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: including says the large letter goes inside the articles

parts.note: the is the definite article
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A note is found under articles including a large jumper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumper' looks like a sweater, given L for large, but it is a high jumper.
explanation.definitionFit: A high jumper or long jumper is a track-and-field sportsperson.

clue.text: Teasing clothes in set excited husband

parts.note: kit means clothing or gear

indicators.note: excited signals the letters of in set are agitated

explanation.surface: A husband teases by putting clothes into a set.
explanation.definitionFit: Kittenish means playful or flirtatious.

clue.text: Part of leg, in tango, elevated

parts.note: T is tango in the radio alphabet
high means elevated

explanation.surface: A dancer raises a leg in the tango.
explanation.definitionFit: The thigh is the upper section of the leg.

clue.text: Physicist nothing like a muscleman?

parts.note: Ernst Mach was an Austrian physicist
O resembles zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A physicist is unlike a strong man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nothing like' reads as 'not at all like', but 'nothing' is O.
explanation.definitionFit: Macho means aggressively masculine, like a body-builder.

clue.text: Trap leader of spies revealed, initially hidden

parts.note: M is the head of the secret service in Bond stories
out means revealed

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of hidden

explanation.surface: A spy chief is exposed after being concealed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trap' is slang for mouth, as in 'shut your trap'.
explanation.definitionFit: Trap is slang for the gob, as in 'shut your trap'.

clue.text: New department's report

parts.note: Oise is a department of France

explanation.surface: A new department's report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Report' means a bang.
explanation.definitionFit: A report is a loud bang, a sound.

clue.text: Old partner and I have to accept end of alliance with wounded director

indicators.note: to accept means taking in, so the pieces go inside

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
I is taken as written
've is the short form of have

indicators.note: end of points to the last letter of alliance

parts.note: cut means wounded

explanation.surface: An ex-partner must accept the alliance's end with a wounded director.
explanation.walkthrough: EX + I + VE take in E + CUT.
explanation.definitionFit: An executive is a senior manager of a company.

clue.text: Although receiving support, long to be without hard liability

indicators.note: receiving means the word for although takes in the support

parts.note: while can mean although
a tee supports a golf ball

indicators.note: without means outside, so the yearning goes round the hard letter

parts.note: to long is to pant
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Although holding up, someone longs to be rid of a hard debt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' means outside: PANT goes round H.
explanation.definitionFit: A white elephant is a costly possession that is more trouble than it is worth.
